name: HI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 urban Honolulu seat with incumbent Ed Case running again
Case has raised about $1.1M; no reported fundraising for the Republican challenger
No public polls or expert ratings; prediction markets price a Democratic win near 96%
Green and independent candidates on the ballot may trim the two-party margin slightly
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Case: a strongly Democratic district, an established incumbent, and a large financial edge over a little-known challenger with no visible fundraising. With no polling available, the margin rests on district lean and incumbency, which support a Safe D rating.
model.watch: Any late-arriving polling or signs of serious challenger fundraising would be the first indication the race is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Hawaii's 1st District covers urban Honolulu and leans Democratic by 13 points. Ed Case, the incumbent Democrat, is seeking another term and has raised about $1.1 million with roughly $600,000 on hand. Republican Adriel Lam shows no reported fundraising, and Green and independent candidates also appear on the ballot. No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race, and prediction markets put Democratic chances around 96 percent.

The combination of a strongly Democratic seat, an established incumbent, and a large money advantage makes Case a heavy favorite. The main source of uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves room for the final margin to land wider or narrower than fundamentals suggest, though a Republican upset would require a substantial and unexpected shift.
